overview.title: Pack OpenWebText into token binaries
overview.summary: Download OpenWebText, mark document boundaries, and write the binaries a full GPT-2 run trains on.

sections.title: Download, mark documents, and save bins
sections.pseudocode:
Download openwebtext with 8 workers and hold out a fraction 0.0005 with seed 2357.
Encode with the gpt2 tokenizer and append end-of-text id 50256.
Write each split as uint16, below 2**16, in 1024 shards.
# Insight: This is the dataset the default train.py settings expect.

logic.title: Pack OpenWebText into token binaries
logic.summary: Download OpenWebText, encode it with the GPT-2 tokenizer, and write one memory-mapped binary per split.

sections.title: Download the corpus and hold out a tiny validation set
sections.pseudocode:
Use 8 worker processes to load and to map.
Load the gpt2 tokenizer.
When run as a script, download the openwebtext dataset.
Hold out a test fraction of 0.0005, shuffled with seed 2357.
Rename that holdout to val.
# Context: The source notes this download is large, on the order of the Hugging Face cache for the whole corpus. Only the main process does it.

sections.title: Append an end-of-text id to every document
sections.pseudocode:
Encode each document's text, ignoring special tokens.
Append the end-of-text id. For gpt2 that id is 50256.
Keep the ids and their length.
Map that function over both splits with the same 8 workers.
# Inferred: The comment wonders whether the end-of-text id should be prepended instead. The code appends it.

sections.title: Write each split into a uint16 binary
sections.pseudocode:
Sum the document lengths as uint64.
Open a memory map named for the split, in write mode.
Store tokens as uint16, which fits because 50256 is below 2**16.
Write the ids in 1024 contiguous shards.
Flush the map.
# Insight: train.py memory-maps these same bins. It does not read the original documents.
